classification.difficultyReason: Swap coordinates of useful points and reconstruct each reflected graph, preserving both parabola branches and converting the exponential's horizontal asymptote into a vertical one.

content.prompt: Sketch the reflection of these graphs across $y=x$.

spec.description: Unit grid with the supplied straight line and dashed reflection axis.
spec.mathematics: y=x/2+1; Cartesian grid from -5 to 5 on both axes.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied reflected line is excluded.

answer.worked: Exchange the coordinates: $(0,1)$ becomes $(1,0)$ and $(2,2)$ stays fixed. Draw the straight line through these points, continuing in both directions. Its equation is $y=2x-2$.

spec.description: Reflected straight line on the original coordinate frame.
Unit grid with the supplied straight line and dashed reflection axis.
spec.mathematics: y=2x+3; Cartesian grid from -5 to 5 on both axes.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied reflected line is excluded.

answer.worked: Exchange the coordinates: $(0,3)$ becomes $(3,0)$ and $(-3,-3)$ stays fixed. Draw the straight line through these points, continuing in both directions. Its equation is $y=\dfrac{x-3}{2}$.

spec.description: Reflected straight line on the original coordinate frame.
Unit grid with the single distinguishable descending line and dashed reflection axis.
spec.mathematics: y=1-x; Cartesian grid from -5 to 5 on both axes. The reflection coincides with the original.
spec.answerVisibility: The original descending line remains visible.

answer.short: $y=1-x$; the reflection coincides with the original line.
answer.worked: Exchange the coordinates: $(0,1)$ becomes $(1,0)$ and $(1,0)$ becomes $(0,1)$. The reflected line passes through the same two points, so it coincides with the original line $y=1-x$.

spec.description: Reflection coinciding exactly with the original descending line.
Unit grid with an upward-opening parabola and dashed reflection axis.
spec.mathematics: y=x^2, vertex (0,0); Cartesian grid from -5 to 5 on both axes.
spec.answerVisibility: Both supplied reflected branches are excluded.

answer.worked: The vertex $(0,0)$ stays fixed. Exchange the coordinates: $(-1,1)$ becomes $(1,-1)$ and $(1,1)$ stays fixed. Draw a smooth right-opening parabola through these points, with both branches continuing rightwards. The reflected relation is $x=y^2$.

spec.description: Both branches of a right-opening parabola.
spec.mathematics: x=y^2, x>=0 and y in R.

spec.description: Unit grid with an increasing cubic and dashed reflection axis.
spec.mathematics: y=x^3; Cartesian grid from -5 to 5 on both axes.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied cube-root reflection is excluded.

answer.worked: The points $(-1,-1)$, $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$ stay fixed. Exchange the coordinates of other points: $(-\tfrac12,-\tfrac18)$ becomes $(-\tfrac18,-\tfrac12)$ and $(\tfrac12,\tfrac18)$ becomes $(\tfrac18,\tfrac12)$. Draw the smooth reflected curve through these points, continuing in both directions. Its equation is $y=\sqrt[3]{x}$.

spec.mathematics: x=y^3, equivalently y=cube root of x; domain and range R.

spec.description: Unit grid with an increasing exponential and dashed reflection axis.
spec.mathematics: y=2^x, passing through (0,1), (1,2), (2,4), approaching y=0 from above; Cartesian grid from -5 to 5 on both axes.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied logarithmic reflection is excluded.

answer.worked: Exchange the coordinates: $(0,1)$ becomes $(1,0)$, $(1,2)$ becomes $(2,1)$ and $(2,4)$ becomes $(4,2)$. Draw a smooth increasing curve through these points. The horizontal asymptote $y=0$ reflects to the vertical asymptote $x=0$, approached from the right. The reflected curve is $x=2^y$.

spec.description: Increasing logarithmic curve approaching the y-axis from the right.
spec.mathematics: x=2^y, equivalently y=log_2(x); x>0, y in R, vertical asymptote x=0.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; no extra printed asymptote label.

spec.description: Unit grid with a translated upward-opening parabola and dashed reflection axis.
spec.mathematics: y=x^2-4, vertex (0,-4), x-intercepts (-2,0) and (2,0); Cartesian grid from -5 to 5 on both axes.
spec.answerVisibility: Both supplied reflected branches are excluded.

answer.worked: Exchange the coordinates: the vertex $(0,-4)$ becomes $(-4,0)$, $(-2,0)$ becomes $(0,-2)$ and $(2,0)$ becomes $(0,2)$. Draw a smooth right-opening parabola through these points, with both branches continuing rightwards. The reflected relation is $x=y^2-4$.

spec.description: Both branches of a right-opening parabola with vertex (-4,0).
spec.mathematics: x=y^2-4, x>=-4 and y in R.

spec.description: Unit grid with a circle and dashed reflection axis.
spec.mathematics: Circle centred at (2,0), radius 2, equation (x-2)^2+y^2=4; Cartesian grid from -5 to 5 on both axes.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied reflected circle is excluded.

answer.worked: Exchange the coordinates of the centre: $(2,0)$ becomes $(0,2)$. Reflection preserves the radius, so draw a circle of radius $2$ centred at $(0,2)$. It passes through $(-2,2)$, $(2,2)$, $(0,0)$ and $(0,4)$.
